content: Overview {{snippet.EventItem_MainEventTicketAbout}} Pre-requisite for Sandboxes If you create an {{variable.Object_EventItem}} with {{variable.Field_EventItem_Address}} set to “Optional” or “Required” in a Sandbox, you must set the {{variable.Field_EventItem_Country}} field to “Required.” You will get an error if the {{variable.Field_EventItem_Country}} field is set to “Hide” (default setting). Create a Main Event Ticket 1. From a New Event Item window, add the following information in each section. Information & Description {{snippet.EventItem_InfoAndDescription}} Availability & Limits Enter information about the sales start/end dates. {{variable.Field_ETEventItem_SalesStaDate}} {{variable.Field_ETEventItem_SalesEndDate}} {{variable.Field_ETEventItem_SalesStaTime}} {{variable.Field_ETEventItem_SalesEndTime}} Capacity & Waitlisting {{snippet.EventItem_CapacityWaitlisting}} Attendee Form There are multiple fields on the Attendee Form that you can hide, make required, or show as optional for each Main event ticket. For example, if you have a "Child Under 3 Yrs" ticket for sale, it is unlikely that the child has an email address. Therefore, you can hide the {{variable.Field_EventItem_Email}} field from this {{variable.Object_EventItem}} 's Attendee Form. {{snippet.EV_EventItem_Create_AttendForm}} Live Attendee Form Example 2. Click Save & New to create a new {{variable.Object_EventItem}} or click {{variable.Button_Save}} . Create a Guest Ticket Configure Guest Tickets Guest Tickets give Event Organizers flexibility in how they collect and manage guest data. There are three configuration options available: Create a {{variable.Object_Contact}} Record: This option allows you to create {{variable.Object_Contact}} records for each guest. Do Not Create a {{variable.Object_Contact}} Record: Select this option if you prefer not to create guest {{variable.Object_Contact}} records. Allow Anonymous Guest Registration: This option enables guests to register without providing their personal information. Please take a moment to review when to use each option and how it works. Configuration Options Create Contact Records for Guest Attendees Creating a {{variable.Object_Contact}} record for each guest {{variable.Object_Attendee}} ensures that every individual has a corresponding {{variable.Object_Contact}} record, even when only minimal information is provided. When to use this option: Your organization requires a {{variable.Object_Contact}} record for each {{variable.Object_Attendee}} . It is important to maintain relationship tracking between {{variable.Object_Contact}} s. Complete attendance records are essential for accurate reporting. You plan to collect full guest contact details at some point after the registration process. How it works: The Event Organizer checks the {{variable.Object_EventSettings}} {{variable.Field_EVSetting_CreContGuestTi}} checkbox. If a guest’s information is incomplete, the system will automatically: Generate the {{variable.Field_Contact_LastName}} value as "[Primary Registrant's {{variable.Field_Contact_LastName}} ] Guest [Number]" (e.g., "LastName Guest 1, LastName Guest 2"). Use the primary registrant's email if the guest’s email is not provided. This process prevents REQUIRED_FIELD_MISSING errors while ensuring that {{variable.Object_Contact}} records are created. Skip Contact Creation for Guest Attendees Not creating a {{variable.Object_Contact}} record for guest {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s creates an {{variable.Object_Attendee}} record but doesn't create the corresponding {{variable.Object_Contact}} record. When to use this option: You don't need relationship tracking for guest {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s. {{variable.Object_Attendee}} records are sufficient for your {{variable.Object_Event}} reporting. You collect minimal information for guests during registration. How it works: The Event Organizer unchecks the {{variable.Object_EventSettings}} {{variable.Field_EVSetting_CreContGuestTi}} checkbox. The system will create {{variable.Object_Attendee}} records for guests. The system will NOT Create {{variable.Object_Contact}} records for guests. Evaluate relationship settings for guests. Allow Anonymous Guest Attendees This configuration offers the most flexibility by enabling fully anonymous guest registrations. When to use this option: You want to allow "plus one" guest registrations. You don't need to collect any information from guests. You want to avoid sending confirmation emails to guests. How it works: The Event Organizer unchecks the {{variable.Object_EventSettings}} {{variable.Field_EVSetting_CreContGuestTi}} checkbox. They set the Attendee Form fields for the guest Event Item to "Optional" or "Hidden." If the {{variable.Field_Attendee_Email}} field is hidden or left empty: No email will be stored on the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} record. A confirmation email will not be sent to the guest. If the {{variable.Object_EventSettings}} {{variable.Field_ETSetting_1UniqAttEmail}} field is checked, guests will be exempt from this rule, and the duplicate email error will not be triggered. Tips Data Needs: Choose a configuration that balances your need for complete {{variable.Object_Contact}} data with the desire to avoid creating unnecessary records. Email Communication: Note that with the first two options, if a guest's email address is the same as the primary registrant's, the confirmation emails for both the primary and guest registrants will be sent to that email address. Attendee Form Settings: Configure the checkout Attendee Form fields ( {{variable.Field_ETAttendee_FirstName}} , {{variable.Field_Contact_LastName}} , {{variable.Field_Attendee_Email}} , etc.) on the {{variable.Object_EventItem}} based on the information you need to collect from guests. Required: The field must be filled in. Optional: The field can be left blank. Hidden: The field is hidden from the registrant. Start Here After creating a Main event ticket, open a New Event Item window and enter the following information to create a guest Ticket. Information & Description Enter a {{variable.Field_ETEventItem_PublicItemNa}} (required). Select an {{variable.Field_ETEventItem_Event}} . Is the Guest ticket free or paid? If it is paid, enter the amount in the {{variable.Field_ETEventItem_Price}} field. If the Guest ticket is free, check {{variable.Field_ETEventItem_Free}} . Set {{variable.Field_ETEventItem_Type}} = "Guest". Select a {{variable.Field_ETEventItem_VisibilityCo}} , if using. Check {{variable.Field_ETEventItem_WaitlistEnab}} to enable waitlisting. Enter a {{variable.Field_ETEventItem_Description}} . Availability & Limits Enter information about the sales start/end dates. {{variable.Field_ETEventItem_SalesStaDate}} {{variable.Field_ETEventItem_SalesEndDate}} {{variable.Field_ETEventItem_SalesStaTime}} {{variable.Field_ETEventItem_SalesEndTime}} Capacity & Waitlisting Enter the {{variable.Field_ETEventItem_QuantityAvai}} . If the field is left blank, the {{variable.Field_ETEventItem_QuantityAvai}} will say “999,999”. The {{variable.Field_ETEventItem_QuantiRemain}} field updates automatically based on the equation, {{variable.Field_ETEventItem_QuantityAvai}} - {{variable.Field_EventItem_RegistQuantity}} = {{variable.Field_ETEventItem_QuantiRemain}} . If waitlisting is enabled, enter an amount in the {{variable.Field_ETEventItem_WaitCapacity}} field, if using. For more information about waitlisting, click here . The {{variable.Field_ETEventItem_Waitlisted}} field will provide a summary of the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s who are waitlisted for the {{variable.Object_EventItem}} . Attendee Form You can customize the Attendee Form for each guest Ticket in several ways. Specifically, you can hide fields, make them required, or mark them as optional. For example, if you have a "Child Under 3 Yrs" ticket, the child is unlikely to have an email address. Therefore, you can hide the {{variable.Field_EventItem_Email}} field from this {{variable.Object_EventItem}} 's Attendee Form. {{snippet.EV_EventItem_Create_AttendForm}} Live Attendee Form Example 2. Click Save & New to create a new {{variable.Object_EventItem}} or click {{variable.Button_Save}} . Important Notes Other Settings Select a previously created {{variable.Object_Form}} or create a new one. Click here for more information about creating {{variable.Object_Form}} s and {{variable.Object_FormElement}} s. Check {{variable.Field_ETEventItem_Hidden}} if you would like to hide the {{variable.Object_EventItem}} from the {{variable.Object_Event}} checkout process. To set a minimum or a maximum number of {{variable.Object_EventItem}} s allowed per order, enter the amounts in the {{variable.Field_ETEventItem_MaxQuantity}} and/or {{variable.Field_ETEventItem_MinQuantity}} fields. An {{variable.Object_EventItem}} ’s {{variable.Field_ETEventItem_QuantiRemain}} will show on the registration page only when there are 10 or fewer {{variable.Object_EventItem}} s available. The {{variable.Field_ETEventItem_MaxQuantity}} or number of Event Items that can be purchased at one time cannot be larger than 10. Please contact {{variable.Link_BlackthornSupport}} if you would like to increase the number to 25. Enter a value in the {{variable.Field_EVItem_DefaultQtySelecti}} field to define the default quantity of Tickets, Guest Tickets, or Products that will be automatically added to the cart when an {{variable.Object_Attendee}} reaches the ticket selection step. If the number of remaining tickets is greater than 0 but less than the {{variable.Field_EVItem_DefaultQtySelecti}} , all remaining tickets will be added to the cart. For example, if the number of remaining tickets is 3, but the {{variable.Field_EVItem_DefaultQtySelecti}} is “5,” then 3 tickets will be added to the cart. If the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} changes the number of tickets in their cart, they can move around the {{variable.Object_Event}} ’s webpage, and no changes will be made to their cart based on the default quantity. NOTE: When an {{variable.Object_Attendee}} purchases Tickets, Guest Tickets, or Products from their AttendeeLink, the default quantity will not be added to the cart. (The original behavior is unchanged.) Event Items Add Custom Fields to the {{variable.Picklist_EventItem_Ticket}} page layout by completing the following steps: Navigate to Salesforce Setup > Object Manager. Search for and click on the {{variable.Object_EventItem}} object. Click "Field Sets." Click on "Blackthorn | Events Wizard Ticket Fields." Drag and drop a field into the list. To make the field required, hover over the field listed "In the Field Set" and click the wrench. Click {{variable.Button_Save}} . Add the {{variable.Field_EventItem_SortOrder}} field to the {{variable.Object_EventItem}} page layout to be able to re-organize the order of the {{variable.Object_EventItem}} s on the registration page. Then, select the order for each {{variable.Object_EventItem}} .   {{variable.Object_Session}} s will not be displayed during registration when the {{variable.Object_Event}} ’s {{variable.Field_ETEvent_UIExperience}} = {{variable.Picklist_Event_UIExp_FullWidth}} , and there is only one free {{variable.Object_EventItem}} with {{variable.Object_Session}} s. Sessions {{variable.Object_Session}} fields can be modified in-line or on the "Sessions Table." Add or remove {{variable.Object_Session}} fields by completing the following steps. Navigate to Salesforce Setup > Object Manager. Search for and click on the {{variable.Object_EventItemSession}} object. Click "Field Sets." Click on "Blackthorn | Events Wizard Event Item Session Fields." Drag and drop fields into the list. To make a field required, hover over the field listed "In the Field Set" and click the wrench. Click {{variable.Button_Save}} .
